newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close at new high, fuelled by banks.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close at new high, fuelled by banks.

text.p: Swedish shares closed at a new all-time high on Monday, fuelled by a flurry of activity in the banking sector and a strong forestry sector.
The Stockholm general index rose a solid 1.09 percent to 2,642.74 in a fairly active day's trade with shares worth 4.35 billion crowns changing hands.

The focus was on the banking sector after Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced they were in merger talks. Trading in both banks was suspended early Monday with details to be released at 0845 GMT Tuesday.
"There is a lot of synergies in the merger," said on broker. "Out of a total workforce of about 14,000 staff there could be as many as 4,000 let go."
Handelsbanken rose eight to 201 crowns after announcing it had secured over 98 percent of shares in mortgage bank Stadshypotek. This completed its 22.9 billion takeover bid.
Some analysts said these mergers could push S-E-Banken and Nordbanken back into merger talks which collapsed two weeks ago.
"It could get them back to the drawing board," a broker said.
S-E-Banken shares closed 2.5 higher at 75 crowns while Nordbanken shares rose two to 235 crowns.
The forestry sector posted strong gains, rising 1.896 percent and continuing last week's upward trend. MoDo jumped 9.5 crowns to 233.5 crowns and AssiDoman rose 3.5 to 190.

Trading in construction and real estate companies NCC, Siab, and Lundbergs was suspended. The Stockholm bourse said more information would be released on Tuesday. Analysts forecast NCC was buying Siab.
Bluechips ended higher. Telecoms Ericsson rose 4.5 to 250 crowns and drugs company Astra up 5.5 to 363.

Airline SAS closed on crown higher at 96.50 crowns after posting a 1996 pre-tax profit of 1.82 billion crowns which was a little higher than expectations. The airline said prices and revenue could come under pressure this year due to tougher competition.
